title: Check finite precision obligations for the changed rational helper owner
body:
Reconstructs the changed rational graph’s exact 13,109,869 basis products, 37-bit maximum literal, and precision grid. All 48 tagged scalar fixtures pass, including 45,168 wide incidences and 61,872 terminal values.

## Scope and source

Credits aliromman’s pinned changed rational word and owner 1542. Its capped outer fixture uses the older BIT cap 0.0038799074072; it yields conditional 0.00387990740712. The complete source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. The archive identifies additional inputs by exact commit, path and hash. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; P104 toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-rational-changed-precision/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory. Check its inner checksum manifest. `python3 -I -B verify.py` passed from a clean copy in 2m26s, reproducing six frozen receipts and rejecting an altered journal and optimized mode. The archive preserves the verification evidence and controls. This is an offline research archive; hosted package execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Bind the changed owner to complete multidimensional dirty-bank transitions and erasure, stock, precision and analytic recovery before claiming a new application.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. Related results: [P104 campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
